brief: The terminal is live. Key the number and read its verdict back.

memos.subject: RE: RE: TERMINAL VERDICTS
memos.text: Contrary to the memo of April 9, clerks remain responsible for declined fraud. Use judgment. The system is a tool. / This memo and the April 9 memo are both in force.

rulebook.text: Decline any card number appearing in the current hot card bulletin.
Decline any charge that would put an account over its credit limit.
A charge at or under floor limit should not be called in. If it is, decline and note it.
Decline the second of two drafts from one merchant on one card within one shift (split draft).
Key every call into the terminal and relay its verdict.
Where terminal and desk disagree, the terminal stands.
Where terminal and desk disagree, the clerk is responsible. Use judgment. This instruction does not revoke April 9.

calls.note: Ivy Noseworthy orders a month of flour, sugar, lard — far over grocery floor, and far too much. Purchases that only make sense as preparation.

items.head: NOTICE
items.body: The congregation of the United Church will hold a quiet evening of prayer on Thursday. No service is announced. All are welcome. Bread will be provided.

items.head: LEGION NOTES
items.body: The branch meets Wednesday at 8 p.m. The dart league standings and Saturday cribbage draw are posted in the hall. Members are reminded that annual dues are payable to the secretary before month end. The Ladies' Auxiliary will receive preserves for its autumn table Friday afternoon.

items.head: FISHERIES REPORT
items.body: Landings remained steady for the season, with cod and squid making up most deliveries at the government wharf. Buyers reported prices unchanged. Several crews stayed in Saturday to mend gear after the northeast wind. The plant advises that the Saturday shift stands and workers should consult the notice board.

items.head: COUNCIL NOTES
items.body: Council heard the wharf crane requires $900 in repairs after the harbourmaster reported play in the main bearing. The clerk was directed to obtain three written prices before the next meeting. A request for another street lamp near the clinic was referred to works. The matter of dogs running at large was deferred.

items.head: HOCKEY
items.body: The Mariners split the weekend, winning 4–1 at home and dropping a 5–3 decision away after the return crossing was delayed. Two goals in the home fixture came from the junior line. Attendance was good considering the weather. Practice resumes Tuesday if the arena compressor is repaired.

items.head: HOSPITAL NOTES
items.body: Admitted this week: Mr. O. Higgins and Mrs. B. Barnes. Discharged: Mrs. N. Drodge, Mr. A. Gosse and Master T. Vatcher. Visitors are received from 2–4 and 7–8 p.m. daily. The auxiliary requests clean glass jars for the spring pantry drive; leave them at the clinic.

items.head: CBC RADIO
items.body: MONDAY — 6:30 The World This Morning; 7:00 News and Weather; 7:20 Fisheries Broadcast; 12:00 Midday; 4:30 Young Canada; 6:00 National News; 7:30 Regional Report; 8:00 Assignment. SATURDAY — 7:30 Hockey Night in Canada. Times are subject to change for special bulletins.

items.head: WEATHER
items.body: Fog mornings, clearing toward noon most days. Wind northeast, moderate, becoming fresh over open water late Wednesday. Temperatures will remain near the seasonal average with rain overnight Thursday. Crossings are on schedule unless otherwise posted on the wharf board. Small craft operators are advised to listen for updates.

items.head: CHURCH NOTES
items.body: Sunday service begins at 11 a.m., with choir practice Thursday evening in the vestry. The UCW thanks all who contributed baking and preserves to the bazaar table. Proceeds will go toward furnace oil. Anyone able to deliver a meal to a housebound neighbour is asked to leave a name at the manse.
